question: Violin virtuoso L Subramaniam is famous for which of the following genres of music globally?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Carnatic music.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• L. Subramaniam, India’s violin icon, “**The Paganini of Indian Classical music**”, and “**the God of Indian Violin**” is the serenity of an Indian musician combined with the captivation of a western star.
 
• Constantly propelled from Singapore to Paris, from Delhi to Los Angeles, he has conquered every followership with the fineness and literacy of his style.
 
• At a very young age, he was honored with the title “**Violin Chakravarthy**” (**emperor of the violin**).
 
• He is trained in the classical Carnatic Music tradition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jazz:**

 
 
• Jazz is a kind of music in which extemporization is generally an important part.
 
• In utmost jazz performances, players play solos that they make up on the spot, which requires considerable skill.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Music:**
 
 
• It is one of the two distinct schools of Indian Classical Music practiced mainly in North India.
 
• The other school of Indian Classical Music is Carnatic music which is practiced mainly in Southern India.
 
• While the historical roots of both the music types belong to the Bharata’s Natyasastra, they diverged in the 14th century.
 
 
 
• **Rock:**
 
 
• Rock music is a broad genre of popular music, frequently defined by its overall meter and aesthetic rather than it's air and musical features.
 
• It began with a gemstone- ‘ n ’- roll and pop in the late 1940s and early 1950s.
 
• Throughout the times, gemstone music spawned dozens of sub-genres, ranging from intricate folk gemstones to death essence and everything in between.
